detail: The S&P 500 closed at 7,688.62 on Wednesday, about 2.0% below its 52-week closing high of 7,844.52, after its best day in three months. It has recovered about half of last week's tech-led dip; small pullbacks like this are normal for a long-term investor.
source: CappNotes and TheStreet closing figures, 4 Nov (high from Reuters, 29 Oct)

detail: Wednesday's rally was wide: across the S&P 500, 400, 600 and Nasdaq-100 members, rising shares beat fallers about three to one (1,122 to 379), and the equal-weight S&P 500 rose more than the normal one. When most shares rise together, a rally rests on more than a few giants.
source: CappNotes closing breadth, 4 Nov (Nasdaq Composite new highs/lows not available)

detail: The US 10-year yield fell about 6 basis points to 4.89%, near its lowest in more than a year, as cheaper oil eased inflation worries. Safe bonds paying nearly 5% still set a high bar for shares to beat.

The Bank of England is widely expected to raise Bank Rate from 3.75% to 4% at noon today, its first rise since 2023. Futures put about a 77% chance on a US Fed rise on 9 December, little changed after the election.
source: CappNotes (CME FedWatch), 4 Nov; IG Bank of England preview, 2 Nov

detail: Brent crude plunged 8.7% to $94.62 a barrel on Wednesday on hopes that pressure to end the Iran war will grow after the US midterms. That is still above the $90 line, so oil keeps nudging inflation and interest rates up, but much less than at $115 last week.
